claim_scope: Dickinson & Pauling (1923) first-page EXCERPT: the mineral molybdenite, MoS2, occurs in hexagonal crystals with basal cleavage, studied by X-ray. Primary-scientific support (excerpt-scoped) for the molybdenite / MoS2 / HEXAGONAL identity underpinning the (later-named) 2H structure. Does NOT establish the modern '2H' label.

locator.system: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 45, 1466-1471 (1923), first-page excerpt image
locator.verbatim: The mineral molybdenite, MoS2, is described as occurring in hexagonal crystals with a very complete basal cleavage. A study of its crystal structure has been carried out using X-ray spectral photographs and Laue photographs.

governance_note: ADMITTED (primary_scientific) via QUAL-JACS-MOLYBDENITE-1923-EXCERPT-001. Excerpt-scoped; the 1923 first page does NOT use '2H'. Same originating work (WORK-DICKINSON-PAULING-1923) as the COD 1010993 record -> NOT independent of it. Contract-C=(not_public,noindex).

source_access_observation.source_classification: The 1925 Caltech dissertation contains a printed reprint of the original 1923 Dickinson–Pauling study; same originating work, not a new independent crystallographic experiment.
source_access_observation.verified_scope: Original paper reproduced in Caltech thesis discusses MoS2 as molybdenite with hexagonal 2-formula-unit cell and c repeat of approximately 12.30 Å; historical terminology cannot be silently relabeled as modern 2H usage in the 1923 text
